verdicts.evidence: On the authors' bundled sim.rda (6000 rows, 1965 events, 6 batches), COLSA's sequential estimates match pooled coxph coefficients within 0.0021 and SE ratios fall in [0.983, 1.021]; fit object size stays flat at ~10 KB across six sequential updates (max/min = 1.06), directly demonstrating constant memory and equivalent efficiency.

Over the full Figure-2 grid K∈{6,20,50,200} with the paper's Appendix-B DGP, COLSA matches Oracle RMSE within 0.001 at every K, clearly beats SGD and Meta at every K, and is the only online method holding ~0.96 coverage at K=200 (Meta 0.793, Online 0.840); the Online baseline is acknowledged as a conservative upper bound (cumulative refit, not true streaming), yet COLSA still overtakes it from K=50 onward.

overall: The logbook establishes both claims through concrete, non-toy experiments: Claim 1 via direct coefficient/SE/memory comparison against the pooled estimator on 6000 rows, and Claim 2 via a from-scratch implementation of the paper's full Figure-2 simulation grid showing COLSA matching Oracle and outperforming online competitors. Limitations (single dataset for Claim 1, upper-bound Online baseline and reduced replication counts for Claim 2) are transparently documented but do not undermine the core findings.
